text: At Alderbrook Wealth Partners, a 140-person registered investment advisor running Microsoft Sentinel, a scheduled analytics rule catches an impossible-travel sign-in on senior relationship manager Teresa Marsh's account. This lesson follows that single alert through triage, scoping, and short-term containment — the exact sequence this capstone's three incident-response lessons prove is one connected system, not three separate skills practiced in isolation.

At 2:47 PM the impossible-travel rule fires: Teresa's account signs in from Atlanta, then from Eastern Europe nine minutes later. Triage rules out a VPN exit node and confirms she isn't traveling. A phone call closes the question — she approved an MFA prompt she hadn't requested, letting push fatigue hand the attacker a valid session.

Opening the investigation graph at 3:05 PM shows more than one flagged sign-in. The Account entity links to a Host entity, WKSTN-FIN-14 — Teresa's own laptop — through a Defender for Endpoint alert raised nine minutes later for a suspicious PowerShell process. The rule that opened this incident never once mentioned that host.

A quick query against SecurityAlert, scoped to that host entity, confirms what the graph showed: a PowerShell process spawned from Outlook, downloading a remote-access tool. Scoping an incident through its graph, not just its opening alert, is what turns one sign-in alert into a two-entity, fully confirmed incident.

At 3:20 PM containment runs in an evidence-safe order, not whatever order feels fastest. Before touching the laptop, Defender for Endpoint's live response captures a memory and disk triage image — volatile data an isolation action would otherwise destroy for good. Only then does the team isolate WKSTN-FIN-14 and disable Teresa's account in Entra ID, revoking its active sessions and refresh tokens immediately.

The incident is contained, not resolved — the scheduled task actually keeping the attacker on this laptop hasn't been found yet. Lesson 30 picks up Monday morning with eradication, a decision about whether to trust this host again, and the after-action report that turns this case into concrete follow-up work.
